clue.text: Difficult prisoner loudly taking drugs

blocks.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
using is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: An awkward inmate is noisily getting high in the cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confusing is hard to follow or understand, so it is a fair synonym for difficult.

clue.text: Caught balls in lid

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a catch taken among the deliveries, oddly tied to a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from cricket: c for caught on the scorecard, and an over being six balls bowled in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover is the top fitted over a pot or box, the same thing as a lid.

clue.text: Raced back with almost half a sea creature

indicators.note: going back means the word for raced is read from its end to its start
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for half is dropped

blocks.note: ran is the past tense of run, to race
w is a standard abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurried home with most of a portion of some marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male carries a long spiral tusk, so it is a sea creature.

clue.text: Overturn northern result

blocks.note: up is used for northward, as in going up north
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A northern election result is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, which is what overturning it means.

clue.text: Popular drink I had lacking flavour

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
to sip is to drink a little
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A trendy drink someone tried turned out to be bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink has little taste, so it describes something without much flavour.

clue.text: Shoot a regiment that's out of order

indicators.note: being out of order means not arranged as it should be, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to fire on a disorderly army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a command to open fire, but it is the botanical verb: to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed that germinates begins to grow and send up a shoot, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Abundant plunder left out

indicators.note: out says something is taken away, so the letter standing for left is removed

blocks.note: to rifle is to ransack or plunder
l is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: There is plenty of loot lying around that nobody took.
explanation.definitionFit: Rife means widespread or plentiful, describing something present in great quantity.

clue.text: Trendy seaside destination with no leader

indicators.note: having no leader means losing whatever stands at the front, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Brighton is a popular seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A fashionable beach town that has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is informal praise for something fashionable or politically correct and up to date.

clue.text: Keep hours of darkness for two weeks

blocks.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort
night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay up through the night for a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb; it is the noun for a castle's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a period of fourteen nights, the British word for two weeks.

clue.text: Foreign watches discussed

indicators.note: something discussed is talked about, so it is the spoken form of the word that counts

blocks.note: to oversee is to watch over or supervise

explanation.surface: Imported timepieces are the topic of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a noun for timepieces; it is the verb to supervise.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas trade or travel is abroad, beyond one's country, which is what foreign describes.

clue.text: Observe red rag waving

indicators.note: a cloth being waved is tossed about, so its letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a matador's red cape flutter before the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at attentively, a close synonym of observe.

clue.text: Tolkien's monster concealed flower

blocks.note: orcs are the brutish creatures of The Lord of the Rings
hid is the past tense of hide, to conceal

explanation.surface: A creature from Middle-earth hid a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is a large family of plants prized for their showy blooms.

clue.text: Yearning to hold one work of art

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: panting for something is longing or yearning for it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone longs to own a single masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a picture made in paint, a standard example of a work of art.

clue.text: Plays for time somewhere in the theatre

blocks.note: first meaning: delays deliberately to gain time
second meaning: the ground-floor seating nearest the stage

explanation.walkthrough: The stalls are the British name for the seats on the main floor of a theatre, the American orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for delaying tactics and as a noun for the lower seating area of an auditorium.

clue.text: Time idiot ran awful convention

indicators.note: awful means badly made, so the following words are knocked into a different arrangement

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: At some point a fool organised a dreadful conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convention' reads as a gathering run by the idiot; it means a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a long-established custom or practice, which is one sense of convention.

clue.text: Trapped by strange instrument

blocks.note: to snare is to catch in a trap
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out by a peculiar device.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched under it that rattle.

clue.text: Means of removing liquid from crushed gardenia

indicators.note: something crushed is squashed out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pressing a gardenia flower to extract its juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is a system of pipes or ditches that carries water away from land or buildings.

clue.text: Criticise old master stealing artist's landscape?

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so the artist ends up inside the words for old master

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
o is the abbreviation for old
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Attacking a classical painter for copying another artist's scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' looks like one phrase for a great painter, but it splits into two abbreviations. The question mark flags that a panorama is a landscape view, not a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view of surrounding scenery, much like a sweeping landscape.

clue.text: Remain too long in public street with a Yankee

blocks.note: out means known publicly
St is the abbreviation for street
taken as written
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American lingers too long out in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay a welcome is to stay beyond the time one is wanted, lingering longer than is proper.

clue.text: Recasts poor player

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters before it come out in a botched arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director replaces a weak performer in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor player' reads as a single phrase for a bad actor, but 'poor' belongs with the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer in a play, and player is an old word for stage actor.

clue.text: Land in eastern nation

blocks.note: e is the abbreviation for eastern
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Territory located in a country in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land owned by one person or family, often with a big house.

clue.text: Hill torn apart in deluge

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor in south-west England
rent is an old past participle of rend, to tear apart

explanation.surface: A hillside is ripped open by a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream or downpour, much like a deluge of water.

clue.text: Republican upset after film showing abuse

blocks.note: a film of moisture is a thin mist
R is the abbreviation for Republican
to eat someone is to worry or upset them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A US politician is angry after seeing a movie about cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' reads as a movie, but it means a thin layer, and 'after' puts that piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat someone is to treat them badly, which is what abuse means as a verb.

clue.text: Calm observed round River Ribble finally

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the others
finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: seen is the past participle of see, to observe
r is the abbreviation for river
the Ribble is a river in north-west England

explanation.surface: A peaceful scene watched beside a Lancashire river at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene describes someone or something tranquil and untroubled, a direct synonym of calm.

clue.text: Southern ice art

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for southern
to ice someone is gangster slang for murdering them

explanation.surface: Ice sculpture from the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice art' looks like a noun phrase for frozen sculpture; 'ice' is a slang verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Art in the older sense of a craft or knack is a learned ability, which is a skill.

clue.text: Husband in pleasant and appropriate situation

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the abbreviation sits within the adjective

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband has found a comfortable and fitting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position that suits someone exactly, a comfortable and fitting place for them.

clue.text: Season some stew in terrine

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a run taken from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of stew, all of in and the start of terrine

explanation.surface: A cook adds seasoning to a stew in an earthenware dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' reads as a cooking verb, but it is the noun for a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is the coldest of the four seasons of the year, between autumn and spring.

clue.text: Nice men struggling with European for prominence

indicators.note: struggling men are thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
e is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Decent men battle alongside a European to gain standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city with a capital letter at the start of the clue, but here it is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is fame or high standing, the state of being distinguished, which matches prominence.

clue.text: Resent heads of exiting nations vacillations year-on-year

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so each of the following words gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Bitterness at countries leaving and wavering every year.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy someone is to begrudge them what they have, feeling the same grudge as resentment.

clue.text: Plant setter keeps in dilapidated toilets

indicators.note: something dilapidated is falling apart, so the letters fall into a different order
keeps means holds inside, so the setter's word wraps around the rest

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword setter has a plant growing in some run-down lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb, but here it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is a parasitic evergreen plant with white berries, hung at Christmas in Britain.
